ai_summary:
Great Britain is recording strong renewable generation today, with total GB wind output reaching 16.6 GW. Scotland plays a pivotal role in this clean power surge, contributing an estimated Scottish wind output of 5.7 GW, which accounts for 56.4% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Thanks to this abundant renewable volume, Scottish carbon intensity has dropped to 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in sharp contrast to the GB-wide figure of 77 gCO2/kWh.

Nevertheless, cross-border transmission bottlenecks prevent this surplus green energy from being fully exported to southern demand centres. Consequently, 14.2 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, running up a constraint cost of about £784,733. To bridge the resulting energy deficit, thermal units downstream were instructed to burn an estimated 2,704,460 m3 of gas, needlessly releasing 4,982 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere.

If sustained at this daily rate, the total yearly cost of curtailment is estimated at £286 million. These balancing expenditures are recovered through system charges, directly impacting consumer bills by adding an estimated £1/MWh to everybody's electricity invoice in the UK.
